# Adjudication Task — Chapter 990

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃990화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|벽력도왕 팽철후.
  6|
  7|하북팽가의 태상가주이자, 정마대전이 낳은 또 한 명의 거인이 쓰러졌다는 소식은 그야말로 성난 들불처럼 퍼져 나갔다.
  8|
  9|“그분만큼은 굳건히 버티시리라 믿었건만……. 기어코 이리되는군.”
 10|
 11|“아무리 그래도 그렇지. 설마하니 도왕(刀王)께서 이처럼 덧없이 떠나실 줄이야.”
 12|
 13|“덧없이? 그런 헛소리는 내 앞에서 두 번 다시 꺼내지 말게. 팽 대협께서는 마지막까지 의기(義氣)를 잃지 않으셨어.”
 14|
 15|“그만하게. 저 친구도 몰라서 한 소리겠나. 그저 안타까워서 하는 소리지.”
 16|
 17|“알고 있네. 빌어먹을. 나도 알고 있다고.”
 18|
 19|생각지도 못한 비보(悲報)를 접한 무림인들은 하나같이 애통함을 감추지 못했다.
 20|
 21|그들에게 있어 십왕(十王)이라는 별호에 깃든 의미는 그만큼 남달랐으니까.
 22|
 23|그러나 모든 이의 존경을 한 몸에 받았던 법왕 굉도도.
 24|
 25|수많은 마교도들을 공포로 몰아넣었던 독왕 당사문도.
 26|
 27|마지막으로 화왕 적천강이라는 압도적인 존재를 제외한다면, 십왕의 실질적인 수좌(隨坐)나 다름없던 벽력도왕마저 죽음을 맞이했다.
 28|
 29|그리고 그들의 사인은 노화로 인한 자연사도, 병사도 아니었다.
 30|
 31|“모두 잊지 말게. 그분들은 협의를 위해 싸우다 명예롭게 전사(戰死)하셨고, 그에 대한 복수는 곧 우리의 몫이라는 것을.”
 32|
 33|정파 무림의 상징이자, 의기의 표상이었던 노강호들의 잇따른 죽음.
 34|
 35|무림인들은 그렇게 애통함이라는 감정 위에 분노를 덧칠했다.
 36|
 37|떠나간 이들의 복수를 위해.
 38|
 39|마교 이후 처음으로 나타난, 그 어느 때보다 위협적인 힘을 드러낸 새로운 적을 쓰러트리기 위해.
 40|
 41|“암천(暗天)과 맞서 싸울 자, 누구인가!”
 42|
 43|“검을 들고 일어나라! 구주천하를 위해, 정의와 협의를 위해 저 천인공노할 악귀들과 맞서 싸우라!”
 44|
 45|거리 곳곳에서 터져 나오는 힘찬 외침들은 이제 예삿일이었다.
 46|
 47|모용세가의 일례를 반면교사 삼은 일파(一派)의 문주와 가주들은 잦은 회동 속에서 묵은 감정을 털어 냈고, 혈기로 들끓는 젊은이들은 피 한 방울 묻혀 보지 못한 병장기를 손바닥이 찢어지도록 휘둘렀다.
 48|
 49|돌멩이가 움직여도 자국이 남는 법인데, 그것이 태산(太山)이라면 오죽할까.
 50|
 51|비좁은 협곡을 사이에 두고 벌어진 산서성에서의 혈전.
 52|
 53|이른바 팔천혈겁(八天血劫)이라 불리게 된 사건과 벽력도왕의 죽음은 마지막 기폭제나 다름없었다.
 54|
 55|아직 정확한 전력이 드러나지 않았음에도 천하 곳곳에서 숱한 피바람을 불러일으키는 암천의 행보에 두려움을 품고 있던 이들도, 일찍이 암천과 맞서는 것에 대해 비교적 미온한 반응을 보이던 정사지간의 무림인들도 이제는 확실히 알게 되었다.
 56|
 57|암천의 손에 들린 저 예리하기 그지없는 칼날이, 정파 무림뿐만이 아니라 천하 전체를 노리고 있다는 것을.
 58|
 59|그리고 그로 인한 파장은, 이제 무림이라는 울타리를 아득히 넘어선 지 오래였다.
 60|
 61|“그래, 어디에서 온 누구인가?”
 62|
 63|“정가촌에서 온 장팔입니다.”
 64|
 65|“장팔? 정가촌에서 왔다면서 왜 장씨야?”
 66|
 67|“예?”
 68|
 69|“왜 장팔이냐고.”
 70|
 71|“아, 그것이…….”
 72|
 73|“그것이, 뭐?”
 74|
 75|“아버지가 외지인입니다.”
 76|
 77|“외지인이라. 그럼 데릴사위라 이거로군. 정가촌에 정착한.”
 78|
 79|“예, 예. 그렇지요.”
 80|
 81|“나이는?”
 82|
 83|“올해로 약관이 되었습니다.”
 84|
 85|모병관으로 임명된 하급 관리는 눈앞의 청년. 아니, 소년이라 불려야 마땅할 지원자를 위아래로 훑었다.
 86|
 87|“약관?”
 88|
 89|“예. 그렇습니다!”
 90|
 91|“그렇군. 그럼 모친의 존함은 어찌 되시나?”
 92|
 93|“예?”
 94|
 95|“이야기를 죽 들어보니 얼굴도 왠지 낯이 익기도 하고, 내가 아는 사람 같기도 해서 말이야. 혹시 아나? 좋은 게 좋은 거라고, 만약 맞다면 전공(戰功)을 쌓기에 괜찮은 곳으로 보내 주지.”
 96|
 97|하급 관리의 은근한 목소리에, 소년의 눈동자가 반짝였다.
 98|
 99|“저, 정말이십니까?”
100|
101|“그렇다니까. 그래서 모친 존함은?”
102|
103|소년은 잠시 망설였지만, 갈등은 그리 길지 않았다.
104|
105|비록 집안의 허락은 받지 못했으나, 마음에 품은 의기와 풍운(風雲)의 꿈은 그 어느 때보다 크게 부풀어 올라 있었다.
106|
107|만약 눈앞의 하급 관리와 부모님이 친분이 있다면, 좋은 전장에 배치되어 눈부신 공적을 쌓아 소년 장수가 될 수도 있는 절호의 기회 아닌가.
108|
109|‘나도. 나도 반드시 그분처럼.’
110|
111|마음의 결정은 이미 내렸다.
112|
113|단 한 번도 본 적 없는 우상을 떠올리며 용기를 얻은 소년은, 어설프게나마 제 손으로 직접 깎아 만든 죽창(竹槍)을 힘껏 말아쥐며 입을 열었다.
114|
115|“그, 감나무 집 오씨댁 둘째 딸이라고 하면 인근에서는 어느 정도 알 거라고 하셨…….”
116|
117|“가라.”
118|
119|“예?”
120|
121|“아버지는 정씨고, 어머니는 오씨인데 왜 정가촌에 살아?”
122|
123|“……!”
124|
125|“왜, 할 말이 남았나?”
126|
127|이미 다 안다는 듯, 날카로운 눈매로 자신을 노려보는 하급 관리의 모습에 경직되어 있던 소년은 가까스로 목소리를 끄집어냈다.
128|
129|“사실 저희 집안 전체가 외지인 출신이라…….”
130|
131|“뭐 하나. 이놈 당장 끌어내!”
132|
133|“헉, 나리! 안 됩니다! 진짜 안 됩니다! 저를 내치시면 진짜 후회하실 겁니다!”
134|
135|소년은 강렬한 의지를 담아 눈을 부릅떴고, 이와 같은 모습에 깊은 감명을 받은 하급 관리는 소년의 양팔을 붙든 관병에게 지시했다.
136|
137|“궁둥이 세 대만 두들겨서 쫓아내게. 약관? 약관은 개뿔이. 어린 놈의 새끼가 어딜 거짓부렁으로도 모자라서 어른한테 눈을 부릅뜨고 있어.”
138|
139|“나리이!”
140|
141|애타게 부르짖었음에도 반전은 없었다.
142|
143|황실의 포고문이 온 천하 곳곳에 퍼진 이후, 입신양명(立身揚名)의 꿈과 끓어오르는 혈기를 참지 못한 이들로 각 성의 관청은 늘 문전성시를 이루고 있었다.
144|
145|그로 인해 암천은커녕 과로로 죽게 생긴 하급 관리는 나이까지 속여 입대하려는 소년들에게 학을 뗀 상황이었으니.
146|
147|“두 대 더 때려!”
148|
149|“안 돼애!”
150|
151|“돼!”
152|
153|결국 관병에 의해 호되게 엉덩이를 걷어차인 소년은 초라하게 쫓겨났고, 관청 밖까지 꼬리에 꼬리를 물고 있던 지원자들은 그 광경을 보며 숙덕였다.
154|
155|“내 동생보다 어려 보이는데.”
156|
157|“그래도 어린놈이 의기가 제법이오. 대가리가 영 빡통인 게 문제지만.”
158|
159|“한데, 저 아이가 어디에서 온 누구라고 했소?”
160|
161|“알아봤자 소용없소. 어차피 지어낸 말이 뻔한데 뭘.”
162|
163|“아니, 그래도 꼭 알아야겠소.”
164|
165|“왜 굳이 그렇게까지 집착하는 거요?”
166|
167|“나도 지어냈으니까.”
168|
169|“…….”
170|
171|“괜히 출신지 지명이 겹치면 안 되잖소. 들키면 나도 저 꼴 날 텐데.”
172|
173|“……혹시 나이가 어찌 되시오?”
174|
175|“열여섯.”
176|
177|“지랄 마시오. 얼굴은 이미 백전노장인데.”
178|
179|“고맙습니다, 형님. 저는 무사히 통과하겠네요. 그리고 이 사실은 비밀로 해 주세요.”
180|
181|“……아니, 농담이 아니었다고?”
182|
183|모두가 충격의 구렁텅이에 빠진 그때, 늙수그레한 용모를 한 지원자가 비틀비틀 일어나는 소년을 향해 말했다.
184|
185|“너, 몇 살이냐?”
186|
187|넋 놓은 눈빛으로 관청을 바라보던 소년이 대답했다.
188|
189|“열여섯입니다.”
190|
191|“나랑 동갑이네. 이것도 인연인데 말 편하게 해.”
192|
193|“지나가는 개새끼도 안 믿을 소리 하지 마십시오. 가뜩이나 기분 더러우니까.”
194|
195|“진짠데.”
196|
197|“안 속아……요.”
198|
199|“그보다 너, 그 창 어디서 났어?”
200|
201|우물쭈물하던 소년이 대답했다.
202|
203|“직접 깎아서……요.”
204|
205|“우리 또래는 보통 검을 쓰지 않나? 나처럼.”
206|
207|그 순간, 복잡하던 소년의 표정이 삽시간에 일그러졌다.
208|
209|“누가 그딴 소리를 해? 창이야말로 만병지왕인데.”
210|
211|“이제야 말을 놓네. 그리고 난 검이 최고라고 한 적은 없어. 그냥 보통은 그렇다는 거지.”
212|
213|“아.”
214|
215|“병장기 문제로 괜히 발끈하는 거 보니까 하나는 알겠네. 너, ‘그 사람’처럼 되고 싶어서 온 거지?”
216|
217|다 안다는 듯이 건넨 물음에, 잠시 머뭇거리던 소년이 훨씬 누그러진 목소리로 대답했다.
218|
219|“그분이야.”
220|
221|“뭐?”
222|
223|“그분. 그 사람이 아니라, 그분이라고.”
224|
225|풀 죽어 있던 모습은 이제 온 데 간 데 찾을 수 없었다.
226|
227|언제 그랬냐는 듯, 소년은 지금 막 관청에서 쫓겨 났다는 사실도 잊은 채 생기 넘치는 눈빛으로 말을 이었다.
228|
229|“열화신룡 진태경. 난 그분처럼 될 거야. 반드시!”
230|
231|누구나 각자가 원하는 목표가 있는 법.
232|
233|소년에게는 진태경이라는 존재가 바로 그런 목표였다.
234|
235|온 천하가 주시하는 강호의 젊은 협객이자, 하늘 같은 천자께서 친히 임명하신 고귀한 열후(列侯).
236|
237|선망했고, 존경했다.
238|
239|당당한 걸음으로 이곳에 올 때까지만 해도, 머지않아 그분과 어깨를 나란히 할 것이라는 포부에 들떠 있었다.
240|
241|물론 현실은 엉덩이를 걷어차여 쫓겨 났지만.
242|
243|“젠장.”
244|
245|소년이 침울하게 고개를 떨군 그때였다.
246|
247|어디선가 낯선 목소리가 불쑥 들려온 것은.
248|
249|“우와! 너무 멋져요!”
250|
251|고개를 들어 목소리의 주인을 확인한 소년은 눈을 깜빡였다. 아니, 관청 밖에서 대기하던 지원자들 모두가 마찬가지였다.
252|
253|‘뭐야, 이 사람은?’
254|
255|‘언제 나타났지? 조금 전에는 없었던 것 같은데.’
256|
257|‘어. 아닌가? 있었나?’
258|
259|‘다시 생각해 보니까 처음부터 여기 있었던 것 같기도 하고…….’
260|
261|얼떨떨하게 주고받는 눈빛과 그 안에 담겨 있는 의문들.
262|
263|하지만 그들이 제대로 된 갈피를 잡기도 전에, 갑작스럽게 모두의 앞에 나타난 청년은 환하게 웃으며 소년을 바라보고 있었다.
264|
265|“제가 할아. 아니, 누구한테 들었는데. 이루고자 하는 목표가 있는 건 좋은 거랬어요!”
266|
267|“예, 예?”
268|
269|소년은 당황 어린 눈빛으로 청년을 바라보았다.
270|
271|먼지로 뒤범벅이 된 장삼(長衫) 때문인지 평범을 넘어 후줄근해 보이는 외모.
272|
273|아마도 그 때문일까.
274|
275|갑작스러운 등장과 안면 트기에 당황스러운 것도 잠시, 경계심보다는 알 수 없는 친근함이 소년을 비롯한 모두를 휘감고 있었다.
276|
277|이건 마치. 마치…….
278|
279|그래.
280|
281|‘동네에 꼭 한 명쯤 있는, 모자란 형.’
282|
283|지금 이 순간만큼은 모두의 생각이 일치했고, 그렇게 믿을 수밖에 없었다.
284|
285|티 하나 없는 저 순백의 웃음을 보라.
286|

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

“That’s so cool! You’re determined to become like the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon. That’s amazing!”

[P142]
With both hands trapped in the young man’s grip, the wide-eyed boy finally came back to his senses when his shoulders began to ache.

[P143]
“P-please let go.”

[P144]
“Oh, sorry. I got excited. Did I hurt you?”

[P145]
You couldn’t spit in a smiling face. Seeing how genuinely worried the young man looked, the boy couldn’t bring himself to complain.

[P146]
“…No, I’m fine. But who exactly are you?”

[P147]
“Just a passing hero who wants to save the world, like you, Young Hero!”

[P148]
He puffed out his chest and declared it proudly. The boy and everyone else reached the same conclusion.

[P149]
*Yep. Definitely slow.*

[P150]
As if to prove them right, the young man kept saying whatever came to mind, oblivious to the change in the air.

[P151]
“But, Young Hero, if you want to become like the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, why come to the government office? You could go straight to the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”

[P152]
“Oh, it’s just so far away. I’ve never been more than a hundred li from home in my life. How could I…?”

[P153]
“It’s far, but not *that* far.”

[P154]
“Not that far? From here in Qinghai to Shanxi?”

[P155]
“You’d get there sooner than you think. Just keep running and don’t give up.”

[P156]
Snickers broke out around them.

[P157]
From Qinghai to Shanxi was nearly ten thousand li, with only a little exaggeration.

[P158]
Even old peddlers who roamed the land with packs on their backs, and even sizable Escort Bureaus, avoided journeys that long whenever they could.

[P159]
The trip would be grueling and mind-numbingly dull.

[P160]
If even people who made their living on the road felt that way, what about those who lived in Qinghai, on the far western edge of the realm?

[P161]
Only a fool would say otherwise.

[P162]
But to a boy whose own impossible dream had drawn laughter, the young man’s words sounded different.

[P163]
“Just keep at it and don’t give up?”

[P164]
“Right! And even if the Jin Family of Taiyuan is too far away, there are other options. For example…”

[P165]
“Do you mean the Kunlun Sect?”

[P166]
“Oh, you know about it?”

[P167]
“Yes. I’m from here. Of course I do. I also know I’m too old to join.”

[P168]
The boy sighed deeply before going on.

[P169]
“But I don’t want to join the Black Dragon Demon Gate. I know it belongs to the Murim Alliance, but its roots are still in the unorthodox faction. There are some unpleasant rumors about it, too.”

[P170]
“Hmm. What about the other sects…?”

[P171]
“The details are different, but it’s much the same with them. I’d rather join the military, learn strategy, and someday become a general leading an army. That might bring me a little closer to his fame.”

[P172]
After pouring all that out, the boy gave a self-mocking laugh.

[P173]
What was the point of telling a complete stranger—one who seemed none too bright—all this?

[P174]
“I should go. Maybe I’ll see you again sometime.”

[P175]
“Hey, wait.”

[P176]
The boy kept trudging off despite the young man calling after him.

[P177]
As the young man watched him go with a dejected expression, a round face popped up beside him.

[P178]
“Hyung, what are you doing here? I’ve been looking all over for you.”

[P179]
The people nearby assumed the bright-eyed child had come looking for the slow older guy. They chuckled and lost interest.

[P180]
They never dreamed that, at that very moment, the adorable child was driving a sinister voice into the young man’s ear—one nobody else could hear.

[P181]
—Didn’t I tell you? Disappear without a word one more time and I’ll kill you. Sword Saint’s Disciple or not, I don’t give a damn.

[P182]
The young man, Cheongpung, answered innocently.

[P183]
—Sorry. I was only going to be gone for a little while.

[P184]
—Were you my enemy in a past life or something? Why do you keep doing this to this old man?

[P185]
—I had a reason.

[P186]
—Then tell me.

[P187]
—I ran out of candied hawthorn skewers[^1].

[P188]
—You little shit…!

[P189]
As he listened to the Slaughter Saint’s deep sigh, Cheongpung watched the boy’s retreating back.

[P190]
Then he thought of someone and smiled to himself.

[P191]
—Hehe. Did I ever tell you? When my Benefactor first met me, the candied hawthorn skewers…

[P192]
—Shut up. Please.

[P193]

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

[P88]

[P89]
“…Wait, you weren’t joking?”

[P90]

[P91]
“How old are you?”

[P92]
The boy stared blankly at the government office.

[P93]
“Sixteen.”

[P94]
“Same as me. Since we’ve met, let’s drop the formalities.”

[P95]
“Not even a stray dog would believe that. I’m in a lousy enough mood already.”

[P96]
“I’m serious.”

[P97]
“I’m not falling for… it, sir.”

[P98]
“Anyway, where’d you get that spear?”

[P99]
The boy fidgeted before answering.

[P100]
“I whittled it myself…”

[P101]
“Don’t people our age usually use swords? Like me.”

[P102]
The boy’s face twisted at once.

[P103]
“Who says that? The spear is the king of all weapons.”

[P104]
“There, you’re talking to me normally now. And I never said swords were the best. I just said most people use them.”

[P105]
“Oh.”

[P106]
“Seeing you get worked up over weapons tells me one thing. You came here because you want to be like ‘that man,’ didn’t you?”

[P107]
The boy hesitated, then answered in a much softer voice.

[P108]
“Show him some respect.”

[P109]
“What?”

[P110]
“Don’t call him ‘that man.’”

[P111]
His dejected look had vanished.

[P112]
As though he’d forgotten he had just been thrown out of the government office, the boy went on, eyes bright.

[P113]
“Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung. I’m going to be like him. I will!”

[P114]
Everyone had a goal they wanted to reach.

[P115]
For the boy, Jin Taekyung was that goal.

[P116]
A young hero of the martial world, watched by the entire land, and a noble marquis personally appointed by the Son of Heaven.

[P117]
He admired him. Respected him.

[P118]

[P119]
Reality, of course, had kicked him in the rear and thrown him out.

[P120]
“Damn it.”

[P121]
The boy lowered his head.

[P122]
Then an unfamiliar voice called out from somewhere nearby.

[P123]
“Wow! That’s so cool!”

[P124]
The boy looked up and blinked at the speaker. Everyone waiting outside the government office did the same.

[P125]
*Who’s that?*

[P126]
*When did he show up? I don’t think he was here a moment ago.*

[P127]
*Huh. Or was he?*

[P128]
*Now that I think about it, maybe he was here the whole time…*

[P129]

[P130]
“My grandpa told me— No, someone told me it’s good to have a goal you want to achieve!”

[P131]
“Y-yes?”

[P132]
The boy stared at him.

[P133]

[P134]

[P135]
It was like… like…

[P136]
Right.

[P137]
*That one slow older guy every neighborhood seems to have.*

[P138]
For once, everyone was thinking the same thing. How could they not?

[P139]
Just look at that spotless, pure-white smile.

[P140]
There wasn’t a speck of malice in his eyes. They were clearer than a stream. Then he grabbed the boy’s hands and shook them over and over, like an excited child.

[P141]
“That’s so cool! You’re determined to become like the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon. That’s amazing!”

[P142]
With both hands trapped in the young man’s grip, the wide-eyed boy finally came back to his senses when his shoulders began to ache.

[P143]
“P-please let go.”

[P144]
“Oh, sorry. I got excited. Did I hurt you?”

[P145]
You couldn’t spit in a smiling face. Seeing how genuinely worried the young man looked, the boy couldn’t bring himself to complain.

[P146]
“…No, I’m fine. But who exactly are you?”

[P147]
“Just a passing hero who wants to save the world, like you, Young Hero!”

[P148]
He puffed out his chest and declared it proudly. The boy and everyone else reached the same conclusion.

[P149]
*Yep. Definitely slow.*

[P150]
As if to prove them right, the young man kept saying whatever came to mind, oblivious to the change in the air.

[P151]
“But, Young Hero, if you want to become like the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, why come to the government office? You could go straight to the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”

[P152]
“Oh, it’s just so far away. I’ve never been more than a hundred li from home in my life. How could I…?”

[P153]
“It’s far, but not *that* far.”

[P154]
“Not that far? From here in Qinghai to Shanxi?”

[P155]
“You’d get there sooner than you think. Just keep running and don’t give up.”

[P156]
Snickers broke out around them.

[P157]
From Qinghai to Shanxi was nearly ten thousand li, with only a little exaggeration.

[P158]
Even old peddlers who roamed the land with packs on their backs, and even sizable Escort Bureaus, avoided journeys that long whenever they could.

[P159]
The trip would be grueling and mind-numbingly dull.

[P160]
If even people who made their living on the road felt that way, what about those who lived in Qinghai, on the far western edge of the realm?

[P161]
Only a fool would say otherwise.

[P162]
But to a boy whose own impossible dream had drawn laughter, the young man’s words sounded different.

[P163]
“Just keep at it and don’t give up?”

[P164]
“Right! And even if the Jin Family of Taiyuan is too far away, there are other options. For example…”

[P165]
“Do you mean the Kunlun Sect?”

[P166]
“Oh, you know about it?”

[P167]
“Yes. I’m from here. Of course I do. I also know I’m too old to join.”

[P168]
The boy sighed deeply before going on.

[P169]
“But I don’t want to join the Black Dragon Demon Gate. I know it belongs to the Murim Alliance, but its roots are still in the unorthodox faction. There are some unpleasant rumors about it, too.”

[P170]
“Hmm. What about the other sects…?”

[P171]
“The details are different, but it’s much the same with them. I’d rather join the military, learn strategy, and someday become a general leading an army. That might bring me a little closer to his fame.”

[P172]
After pouring all that out, the boy gave a self-mocking laugh.

[P173]
What was the point of telling a complete stranger—one who seemed none too bright—all this?

[P174]
“I should go. Maybe I’ll see you again sometime.”

[P175]
“Hey, wait.”

[P176]
The boy kept trudging off despite the young man calling after him.

[P177]
As the young man watched him go with a dejected expression, a round face popped up beside him.

[P178]
“Hyung, what are you doing here? I’ve been looking all over for you.”

[P179]
The people nearby assumed the bright-eyed child had come looking for the slow older guy. They chuckled and lost interest.

[P180]
They never dreamed that, at that very moment, the adorable child was driving a sinister voice into the young man’s ear—one nobody else could hear.

[P181]
—Didn’t I tell you? Disappear without a word one more time and I’ll kill you. Sword Saint’s Disciple or not, I don’t give a damn.

[P182]
The young man, Cheongpung, answered innocently.

[P183]
—Sorry. I was only going to be gone for a little while.

[P184]
—Were you my enemy in a past life or something? Why do you keep doing this to this old man?

[P185]
—I had a reason.

[P186]
—Then tell me.

[P187]
—I ran out of candied hawthorn skewers[^1].

[P188]
—You little shit…!

[P189]
As he listened to the Slaughter Saint’s deep sigh, Cheongpung watched the boy’s retreating back.

[P190]
Then he thought of someone and smiled to himself.

[P191]
—Hehe. Did I ever tell you? When my Benefactor first met me, the candied hawthorn skewers…

[P192]
—Shut up. Please.

[P193]
In Qinghai, the Slaughter Saint was suffering.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
